Bright Data is the better choice for hard targets and enterprise pipelines, where its pool depth, ZIP, ASN and carrier targeting, Web Unlocker and SERP API save real engineering time, and its monthly plans fall to $2.50/GB. Watch for Bright Data's frequent 50%-off promotions, which narrow the gap.

Bright Data and IPRoyal rarely compete for the same buyer, which is exactly why people compare them. Bright Data is the most complete web-data platform on the market, with a 150M+ pool, ZIP and ASN targeting and managed unblocking products. IPRoyal is a value provider whose residential traffic never expires and can be bought one gigabyte at a time. This comparison helps you decide whether your project needs Bright Data's power or whether IPRoyal will do the job for far less.

blocks.text: Bright Data in 2026: what you get

Bright Data is the largest and most complete web-data platform in this market. Beyond residential proxies it sells datacenter, ISP and mobile networks, an unblocking API, a SERP API, a hosted Scraping Browser and ready-made datasets, each billed on its own meter. Its residential network is advertised at more than 150 million IPs in 195 countries, with targeting down to ZIP code and ASN. The trade-off is cost and complexity: the list price sits at the top of the market and the dashboard is built around zones, rules and compliance checks rather than a two-click setup.

Strengths: Deepest targeting in the market (ZIP, ASN, carrier); Managed unblocking, SERP and browser products under one account; Mature compliance and KYC processes that enterprise buyers ask for; Very large residential pool for high-rotation work. Weak spots: Highest list price per GB at low volume; Dashboard and zone setup take time to learn; Some targets need a compliance review before access.
IPRoyal in 2026: what you get

IPRoyal built its reputation on flexible, non-expiring residential bandwidth and straightforward pricing. The pool is smaller than the enterprise networks at 32M+ advertised IPs, but it covers 195 countries, supports SOCKS5, and offers some of the longest sticky sessions available (up to seven days). Its headline $1.75/GB rate only applies at 10 TB; most buyers will pay between $5 and $7 per GB on small orders.

Strengths: Residential traffic that does not expire; Sticky sessions up to 7 days; Can start with a single gigabyte; Several proxy types plus Web Unblocker in one account. Weak spots: Smaller pool than the enterprise networks; Headline $1.75/GB rate needs a 10 TB purchase; Mid-volume prices are not published.
Pricing: Bright Data vs IPRoyal

Bright Data lists residential traffic at $8/GB pay-as-you-go with no commitment, and it frequently runs 50%-off promotions that bring that to about $4/GB. Monthly plans start with the Growth tier at $499 for roughly 141 GB (about $3.50/GB) and fall to around $2.50/GB on the largest public plan.

IPRoyal's residential subscription costs $7 for 1 GB, $11.90 for 2 GB and $52.50 for 10 GB ($5.25/GB); pay-as-you-go is 5% more ($7.35 for 1 GB). The advertised $1.75/GB rate applies only at 10 TB. Prices for custom volumes such as 25, 100 or 500 GB are calculated in the dashboard.

Buying 10 GB, you would pay about $52.50 with IPRoyal and $80 with Bright Data: a 34% saving in IPRoyal's favour. At 100 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because IPRoyal does not publish an exact price for that volume; Bright Data comes to about $499. Look past the per-GB figure too. IPRoyal lets unused traffic carry forward, while Bright Data's allowance does not (monthly plan allowances reset each cycle). For irregular workloads, that difference can outweigh a small gap in list price.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

By advertised size, Bright Data (150M+) is about 4.7x larger than IPRoyal (32M+). Advertised pool sizes are marketing figures counted over long periods; the number of IPs actually reachable in a given country at a given moment is far smaller for every provider, so treat these as a rough guide to depth rather than a guarantee. For coverage, Bright Data lists 195 countries and IPRoyal lists 195. On targeting, Bright Data offers country, state, city, ZIP, ASN and carrier, while IPRoyal offers country, state and city (ISP selection needs verification).
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, Bright Data offers rotating per request or sticky sessions you control per zone, and IPRoyal offers rotating or sticky sessions from 1 second up to 7 days. Setup works the same way on both: a single gateway endpoint, with location and session options passed as username parameters, plus IP whitelisting if you prefer not to use credentials.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: Bright Data wins. The deciding factor for Bright Data: its pool depth and Web Unlocker handle hardened targets. The limitation on the IPRoyal side: solid success rates and non-expiring traffic for bursty crawls.
SERP and rank tracking: Bright Data. Bright Data has the edge here. Why: it sells a dedicated SERP API alongside raw proxies. How IPRoyal compares: it works, but it has no dedicated SERP product.

Social media and multi-account management: IPRoyal. IPRoyal has the edge here. Why: 7-day sticky sessions keep one IP on one account. How Bright Data compares: it is powerful but expensive for low-volume account work.

E-commerce price and stock monitoring: Bright Data wins. The deciding factor for Bright Data: ZIP-level targeting suits local pricing and stock checks. The limitation on the IPRoyal side: city targeting with pay-only-for-what-you-use traffic.

Ad verification and geo-testing: Bright Data. Bright Data has the edge here. Why: carrier and ASN targeting reproduce what real users see. How IPRoyal compares: decent coverage but no ASN or carrier targeting on standard accounts.
Tight budgets: IPRoyal. IPRoyal has the edge here. Why: small entry purchases and traffic that never expires. How Bright Data compares: its list price is the highest in this comparison.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. Bright Data: Free trial for business accounts, no card required. IPRoyal: No general free trial; Enterprise trial for verified companies. Verification and payment rules differ too. Bright Data: Verification required for some sensitive targets. IPRoyal: Optional ID verification; required for ISP-level targeting and PayPal. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test Bright Data and IPRoyal before you commit
Spec sheets only get you so far. A short, structured test on your own targets will settle Bright Data vs IPRoyal faster than any review:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (Bright Data: free trial for business accounts, no card required; IPRoyal: no general free trial; Enterprise trial for verified companies).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.

3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country. 4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, Bright Data comes out ahead in 4, IPRoyal in 2, and 0 are ties. That makes Bright Data the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: Bright Data is strongest for enterprise data teams with budget for managed tooling, while IPRoyal is strongest for irregular or seasonal projects. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
